text: SitRep66 Tableau 6: 734 in isolation at end of day (295 confirmed / 439 suspected, a split that closes exactly against the census) at 78.2% global bed occupancy (734/939 beds); Ituri 69.3% (553/798) after a bed expansion from 706, Nord-Kivu 128.4% (181/141) and saturated; Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND. The bed identity closes exactly at every level (720 J-1 + 108 admissions - 94 exits = 734; Ituri 543 + 70 - 60 = 553; Nord-Kivu 177 + 38 - 34 = 181). Exits over 24h (94 total): 18 deaths, 63 non-cases, 3 recoveries, 10 escapes. Ituri first-line personnel: 121 cumulative infections, 67 recovered (Table 8; the prose says 65), 18 hospitalized, 36 deaths (CFR 29.8%).

text: A NEW health zone was affected: Adja, in Aru Territory, northern Ituri, entering the table at 10 confirmed cases and 1 death in a single cycle rather than as one index case. That takes Ituri to 28/36 and the national roster to 47 zones touched, 46 actively transmitting. A zone that appears at 10 cases was already carrying an established chain when it was detected, so the figure is a floor on what has been happening there, not this cycle's incidence.

text: 79 new confirmed cases (Ituri 70, Nord-Kivu 9) and 37 new deaths (Ituri 35, Nord-Kivu 2) take the DRC cumulative cleanly to 2423 confirmed / 967 deaths (CFR 39.9%) with no harmonization this cycle. Ituri's new cases concentrate at Bunia (18), Nizi (16), Rwampara (10) and the new Adja (10). Laboratory positives (70 + 9 = 79) equal the day's confirmations exactly.

text: Surveillance capacity fell on both axes even as the case count held: contact follow-up dropped to 81.1% (8531/10519) from 85.8%, and Ituri's alert-investigation rate to 75.6% (335/443) from 86.4%, leaving 108 alerts uninvestigated. Haut-Uele investigated 4 of 36 alerts. Both the contact cohort and the contacts seen shrank, and Tshopo stopped reporting contacts while Haut-Uele resumed, so the national coverage figure mixes performance with a change in who reports.
